description:
FILED s473t3 (Opus triage of the 79 CATALOG-only blessed rows), on main
d9a2aac0.  PRE-EXISTING.  Probe: scratch/s473t3/probes/p14-tied-underscore.pl.

ROWS BEHIND IT (baselines/fail-baseline.tsv, 3 rows):
  local.t 258 `Underscore 'Chop'`
  local.t 259 `Underscore 'Filetest'`
  local.t 260 `Underscore 'Assignment'`
  -- perl-tests/local.t:604-626 (the UnderScore package whose FETCH/STORE die)

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl):
    package UnderScore;
    sub TIESCALAR { bless \my $self, shift }
    sub FETCH { die "read  \$_ forbidden\n" }
    sub STORE { die "write \$_ forbidden\n" }
    package main;
    tie $_, 'UnderScore';
    for my $t (['Reading',    sub { print }],
               ['Matching',   sub { my $x = /badness/ }],
               ['Concat',     sub { $_ .= "a" }],
               ['Chop',       sub { chop }],
               ['Filetest',   sub { -x }],
               ['Assignment', sub { $_ = "Bad" }]) {
      eval { $t->[1]->() };
      printf "%-12s died=%d\n", $t->[0], ($@ ? 1 : 0);
    }
  perl: all six died=1
  PCL : Reading 1, Matching 1, Concat 1, Chop 0, Filetest 0, Assignment 0
  The first three are the CONTROL -- scalar tie works in PCL, and read magic
  fires for `print`, a match and `.=`.

THREE MISSES:
  (a) `chop` with no argument -- the implicit-`$_` operand is read without
      get-magic (and written without set-magic).
  (b) a bare filetest `-x` -- the `$_` the s416/#372 default pre-pass splices
      in is read raw.
  (c) `$_ = VALUE` -- a plain scalar assignment to a tied variable does not
      call STORE.  This is the worst of the three: the tie is silently
      bypassed on WRITE, so a `Tie::StdScalar` subclass that validates or
      transforms is simply not consulted.

CATALOG NOTE THIS REPLACES: sweep-bug-catalog.md local.t, "`local $_` with
filetest/match (tests 255-264)" -- MEASURED WRONG: there is no `local` in
these rows at all, and the match spelling PASSES.

FAMILY: scalar tie magic (working; `docs/not-supported.md` "`tie` on an
ARRAY or HASH" / #155 is the container half).  Sibling of #1482, which is the
same "read the box, skip the magic" mistake in the harness.
subject: SILENT WRONG (scalar tie): `chop`, a bare filetest `-X` and a PLAIN assignment do not fire a tied `$_`'s FETCH/STORE -- `tie $_, 'T'; $_ = "Bad"` never calls STORE, where perl does
